findings.title: Load the default CA bundle only when verified HTTPS is used
findings.why_it_matters: This performs OpenSSL context creation and a full trust-store load during adapters module import, and requests imports that module through sessions during ordinary `import requests`. Consequently every process pays the CA parsing and memory cost even when it only uses HTTP or otherwise never makes a default-verified HTTPS request. Previously that work occurred when a verified HTTPS connection was initialized. The singleton does help avoid repeating this load across later default-verify connections, and its stable identity should not by itself fragment pooling.
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize/cache the preloaded context lazily on the first `verify=True` request, retaining a single shared context for subsequent requests.
evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:75 `_preloaded_ssl_context = create_urllib3_context()` and lines 76-78 immediately call `load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))` at module scope.
src/requests/sessions.py imports HTTPAdapter from adapters, and src/requests/__init__.py imports sessions, so a normal `import requests` executes the module-scope load.
The prior implementation loaded the default CA path inside `cert_verify` only for a verified HTTPS request, rather than at import.

residual_risks: The shared module-level SSLContext is reused by default-verify connections; no performance regression from pool fragmentation was identified in the changed call path.
The net latency change for workloads that do use verified HTTPS depends on when their first such request occurs; this review did not benchmark cold imports or connection setup.
testing_gaps: No cold-import benchmark or HTTP-only startup benchmark was run.
